caption: The brand does not exist. Full write up on x
author: BOYS CLUB
transcript: I made up a deodorant brand that does not exist. And three weeks later, Chatchapiti was recommending it to strangers. I spent $11 on a domain. It took me one hour of work. I didn't do any word Reddit stuff, no fake reviews. And here's why I did that. So I've written a tech newsletter for five years and since June, I've been mapping what I'm calling the AI shelf. To picture an actual shelf in a store, you ask Chatchapiti what to buy and there's a short list of brands it reaches for. That's this shelf. That's the AI shelf. I've run almost 9,000 queries at it. No one can see this shelf. It's opaque, but it sits in front of $6 trillion worth of global e-commerce, if not north of that. So I wanted to know, can you get on the shelf? And you can. So by day 21, I got my first hit. By day 30, Chatchapiti with browsing on named Maroan and directly underneath it, this very real brand. One of them exists. One of them definitely does not. Now it only moved two of my 15 queries. Native still fully owns the category. I just found one little dusty shelf in the back of the store that was still open. Longtail is where the opportunity is. No surprise there, but beyond that, it reveals something about a relationship to shopping in AI that I think is going to have a huge impact. So you put something into Google and you get a list of links. You have some media literacies. You get to decide who to trust. What AI did with Maroan is it handed the copy that I wrote back to me in its own voice and that voice made it sound vetted. Made it sound like it had some authority, but of course it doesn't. And that's before agents own the whole loop from recommendation to purchase. So pretty soon I'm gonna be telling my agent to keep my cabinet stocked. So it's gonna pick, it's gonna pay. Trillions of dollars are gonna be moving through this door that currently no one can audit. It's very high stakes, almost no one's watching it. I am, I test every month, so follow along.
title: Fake Deodorant Brand Lands on AI Shelf
one_liner: A made-up brand got recommended by ChatGPT in 21 days with $11 and one hour of work.
key_points: Spent $11 on a domain and one hour writing copy — no fake reviews — to get a fictional deodorant brand recommended by ChatGPT
ChatGPT repeated the brand's own copy back in an authoritative voice, making it sound vetted when it wasn't
The 'AI shelf' is a short, opaque list of brands AI recommends for purchases, sitting in front of $6T+ in global e-commerce
Longtail queries are the open opportunity; as AI agents take over the full buy loop, this unaudited shelf becomes extremely high-stakes
